title: Two quiet moves: choose by the imbalance, not the count
outcomes: Chooses the better of two quiet continuations when material is level
Names one concrete difference between the two resulting positions (an outpost, a file, a pawn shield, space)
Does not let a pawn-winning count decide a comparison without looking at the rest of the position
Sees when two quiet moves are too close to separate and stops comparing

steps.text: In **Compare the positions, not your first idea** and **Compare the end positions: name the feature that decides** you compared end positions. Now both moves are quiet and the material is level, so counting cannot decide. Picture each end position and ask what each move changes: a square for a piece, a file, a pawn, the cover around the king. The list of imbalances is in **Imbalances: fill the list, then use one**.

**Rule of thumb:** name one thing each move changes, then ask which change matters more in this position. The engine's number only says which end position it likes; it does not tell you why. A difference you can name is a candidate reason, not a proven one. This pays once forcing lines are used up and two quiet moves remain.

steps.title: Quiet difference, material trap, no difference
steps.prompt: Predict first: in which position do two quiet moves differ in a way you can name, in which does the pawn-winning move lose the comparison, and in which are the two moves too close to separate? Then check.

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** There is no comparison panel at this level. Hints are offered on request, and silent items turn hints and the engine off. In My games, the review lists the biggest drops; after a drop, write down the two end positions you should have compared. The next three items are silent.
